reviewed_version: arXiv:2207.04251v2, submitted 14 February 2024; title page dated 15 February 2024
summary: Lemma4.7 is false for the actual support-truncated derivative and fractional Brownian increments. The later text already defines the true adjoint and derives conditional duality from it. No direct bridge from the false identity to failure of the quantitative estimate or main theorem has been established; core impact remains Needs Evidence.

problems.claim: Lemma 4.7 Gaussian integration by parts with D_[a,b] defined by support truncation and unchanged W(h).
assumptions: Scalar fBm on [0,1], H=1/3 inside the main range
Smooth cylindrical class permits linear functions and constants
Half-open indicator convention represents the same continuous Gaussian increments
problems.decisive_evidence: D_[a,b]F=D_[a,b]G=0 but E[F G W(h)]=(1-2^(1/3))/2, strictly between -1/6 and -1/8. The finite enclosure is exact by rational cubing.
problems.invalid_step: Support truncation in a covariance Hilbert space is treated as though it preserved the full-derivative inner product with supported h; disjoint fractional increments are correlated.
problems.core_dependency: Established: adjoint definition/product rule/locality -> (28) -> Proposition4.17; Theorem4.11 -> Lemma4.18 and required regularity; Proposition4.17/Lemma4.18 -> Theorem6.1. Not established: false Lemma4.7 identity -> invalid Theorem4.11 estimate. Presentation order alone is insufficient.
counterevidence: Brownian H=1/2 gives zero cross-covariance and does not expose the identity error
No pair of distinct RDE solutions constructed
Section4.3 already defines the actual adjoint of D_[a,b]; (28) is derived from that duality, product rule and locality, without the false W(h) identification
No counterexample to Theorem4.11's domains/constants or its cited use was established
Authors have linked an erratum, whose contents remain unavailable
problems.correction: For a bounded restriction P and appropriate domains, the deterministic Gaussian term is W(P* h), and the adjoint is delta(P* u). Preserve the source's existing adjoint definition; no replacement of (28) or quantitative framework is claimed necessary or proved here.
problems.correction_limits: The conditional operator calculation is not a complete domain or uniform-estimate verification. Core proof damage remains unestablished. Erratum unassessed; no assertion that the current corrected theorem is false.
problems.author_adoption: Erratum existence documented; whether it addresses P1 unassessed
problems.impact: Confirmed erroneous local identity in acquired v2; Minor on available evidence. A material effect on the central regularizing estimate would require further direct evidence.

independent_verification.result: Confirmed local false identity: for fBm H1/3, F=B_(1/2),G=1,h=1_(1/2,1], both restricted derivatives vanish but E[FGW(h)]=(1-2^(1/3))/2 lies strictly between -1/6 and -1/8. The smooth cylindrical class allows F and G. For bounded P and appropriate domains the deterministic adjoint term is W(P* h). Counterevidence read: Sections4.3-4.4 already define divergence by adjoint duality and derive (28) without the false W(h) term. Proposition4.17 uses (28), and Theorem4.11 is expressly used in Lemma4.18; no invalid Lemma4.7-to-Theorem4.11 derivation or counterexample to those quantitative estimates was established.

clarifications.evidence: Same initial point and sigma=1, constant drifts 0 and 1 give path difference t>0; printed right side negative. Earlier Theorem 2.10 pp.14-15 has plus sign.
clarifications.correction_limits: Plus sign removes this display contradiction; does not repair the Gaussian-calculus issue.

decisive_checks.result: s=κ+1/α-3ε/8, ν=1/2+ε/8 imply s+ν>2 iff κ+1/α>3/2+ε/4; α=2H gives threshold with strict slack.
decisive_checks.limitation: Only arithmetic checked, not the stochastic bound supplying s,ν.

focused_acceptance_summary.scope: Focused independent challenge of the existing Lemma4.7 claim and its alleged core dependency. The covariance counterexample is confirmed under the actual global polynomial-growth cylindrical class and support restriction. Actual adjoint and conditional-duality derivations were read, and the unsupported bridge from Lemma4.7 to failure of Theorem4.11 was removed. No new unrelated defect search, quantitative-estimate audit, erratum reading or journal-version equivalence is claimed.
focused_acceptance_summary.assessment_review: Correct overall and P1 from Major to Minor for the established local identity error. A material failure in the main quantitative proof remains Needs Evidence: the source already defines the true adjoint and (28) uses that definition, product rule and locality; adjacency of Lemma4.7 and later statements is not a proved dependency. This neither certifies Theorem4.11 nor asserts that the current corrected theorem is defective.
